pins.note: normally closed contact

typ.conditions: rated coil current at 5 VDC, L type 0.36 W, 20 °C: first row (05) of the coil table, which the text layer splits into columns

current.note: coil current at the rated 5 V; the coil resistance is 70 Ω ±10 % (same table)

evidence: As a countermeasure, install surge absorbing circuits at both ends of
the coil or select a model
requires.note: diode across the coil, cathode to the coil supply; its average rectified current must exceed the coil current (Omron relay precautions p. 9)

hazards.text: Keep the contact side at 60 V DC or less (Circuit Bench is low voltage only); never switch mains.

notes.text: Coil power 0.36 W (L) or 0.45 W (D); SL = sealed, 0.36 W.
Pick-up voltage 75 % max and drop-out voltage 10 % min of the rated coil voltage; max allowable 130 %.
Contact form 1C (SPDT): COM, NO, NC; max switching voltage 250 VAC.
The Songle data sheet does not state a flyback diode; Omron's general relay precautions require surge absorption at the coil.
evidence: Counter electromotive force generated from a coil when the coil is
turned OFF causes damage to semiconductor

notes.text: The coil current is far above what a GPIO can source: drive the coil with an NPN/MOSFET low-side switch or a ULN2003 channel (calc npn / mosfet) and put a flyback diode across the coil.

Relay modules (1/2/4 channel boards) add a transistor or PC817 driver, flyback diode, LED and often a JD-VCC jumper; their inputs are often active low and pulled up to 5 V, so a 3.3 V GPIO may not switch them off reliably. None of this is in the relay data sheet.
